aggregation: ratio of summed numerator and denominator
classes_note: Each class sums its codes of the NAICS edition the file uses (naics-map.json). Classes are not mutually exclusive; never sum across classes. A class absent from a geography that is in values has zero establishments there: CBP lists every industry cell that has an establishment, so absent cells are true zeros and are left out to keep the file small.

flags.cbp-cells-withheld: CBP does not publish every 6-digit cell at county and metro level (charter trap 3). A class code with no 6-digit cell at the geography may hold establishments its published parent industry shows: up_to is the parent's establishments less its published 6-digit children, summed over the class's absent codes; the parent of a code in sectors 31-33, 44-45 and 48-49 is the sector range the API publishes. Such a cell is written [value, up_to]: the value is a lower bound in the series' own unit; up_to is always a count of ESTABLISHMENTS that may be withheld, in cbp_emp and cbp_estab_per_10k as well (it does not bound employees or the rate). scripts/markets.py prints only the value, only with allow_flag, and the page must say "at least".

label: Establishments per 10,000 residents: CBP 2023 establishments over the PEP V2023 estimate for July 1, 2023
naics_edition_note: The CBP files carry NAICS 2017 codes (54 codes that exist only in NAICS 2017 found, 0 only in NAICS 2022), so each class sums its NAICS 2017 code list from naics-map.json.
